newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Cochlear says no plans to reduce R&D.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Cochlear says no plans to reduce R&D.

text.p: Bionic ear maker Cochlear Ltd said it has no plans to reduce its commitment to research and development (R&D) following the government's change in the tax concession rate for R&D spending in last week's federal budget.

Cochlear chairman David Penington said in a statement that the group currently spends over A$11 million or 15 percent of revenue on R&D. Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said the R&D tax concession would fall to 125 percent from 150 percent.
"We do not intend to reduce our commitment to R&D, however this measure will limit our ability to grow the proportion of revenue expended on research in the future," Penington said.
Cochlear earlier reported a net profit to A$10.86 million for the year to June 30, 1996, up five from the A$10.38 million forecast in its prospectus.
Managing director Catherine Livingstone said in a statement that the company had established itself as a profitable company since it listed on December 4, 1995.
"With the total world market for cochlear implants expanding, we continue to focus on increasing the penetration with our markets and growing their overall size," Livingstone said.
At 12.40 p.m. (0240 GMT), Cochlear shares were one cent up at A$3.39 on thin volume.
